newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Heinz chief O'Reilly seen planning slow exit.
newsitem.headline: Heinz chief O'Reilly seen planning slow exit.

text.p: H.J. Heinz boss Anthony O'Reilly plans a slow exit from the multinational corporation, sources close to the company said Tuesday.
Heinz President William Johnson is the front runner in the race to succeed the 61-year-old O'Reilly, a former international rugby star.
Johnson, appointed president of the company in 1996, has been challenged with the task of orchestrating the giant food company's restructuring, and O'Reilly's departure depends on how well it goes.
"I think you are looking at another two to three years before he retires. Johnson is only president for a year and it all depends on how successful the restructuring is," the source said.

Heinz will reveal the details of its restructuring plan on Friday to analysts in San Francisco, the source said, adding that he thought it highly unlikely O'Reilly would make any statement on his retirement at the meeting.
An official at Heinz's headquarters in Pittsburgh declined to comment on the rumours, saying, "This is just speculation."
Speculation that the Heinz chief would leave the company heightened last year when O'Reilly was rumoured to be in ill-health. O'Reilly later denied that his health was a source of concern.

"There has been speculation for some time that O'Reilly would retire from Heinz and concentrate more of his time on his considerable Irish interests," one analyst said, noting that O'Reilly, who likes to take a hands-on approach to his businesses, has interests spanning five continents.

O'Reilly is a multi-millionaire married to a shipping heiress -- Chryss Goulandris -- who mixes with multi-millionaires at his palatial home outside Dublin, at the Deauville race track in France and in Manhattan.

O'Reilly's flagship Irish company, media group Independent Newspapers Plc, has become a serious international player in media and communications with interests in Australia, South Africa and New Zealand.
Thirty years ago O'Reilly was an Irish household name as a rugby star who began playing for his country at the age of 19 and set a 1959 scoring record in New Zealand and Australia that still stands.
